The most powerful refutation is that it is impossible to calculate all the consequences of one's acts. Bentham's felicific calculus requires summing intensity, duration, certainty, propinquity, fecundity, purity, and extent across every affected person, and that sum cannot be completed if the consequences themselves cannot all be known. Pain and pleasure being inevitable features of life does not undermine the calculus, because the calculus already treats both as the quantities to be weighed.

CONFIDENCE: 86
